newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders steady.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders steady.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent a lb lower while feeder cattle were called steady, livestock analysts said.

Pressure is seen in live cattle futures linked to a drop in cash cattle values this week and easier tone to wholesale beef prices. Fed cattle prices declined $3 per cwt this week which may prompt further liquidation in the December contract, analysts said.

Technical selling developed in live cattle Thursday when futures broke through a trend line Wednesday. However, the large discount futures hold to cash cattle prices is seen limiting losses, they said.

Cash cattle in central and southern Plains feedlots sold Thursday at tops of $69.00 per cwt while December cattle futures closed at 66.525 cent a lb Thursday. Cattle also sold at a top of $72.50 in a light test in Nebraska Thursday and in Colorado, at $70.00.
Evening of positions is also expected ahead of Friday afternoon's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report, they added.

The monthly report is expected to show feedlot cattle numbers in the seven key states rising to about year-ago levels. Estimates for November 1 on-feed supplies averaged 99.5 percent of a year ago with October placements averaging 105.7 percent and marketings averaging 97.3 percent of last year.
Feeders look steady with a lower CME Feeder Cattle Index likely offset by lower corn futures calls, analysts said.
The latest index was off $0.08 at $64.45 per cwt.
